title: HOTDO G Tee
summary: Is it a Hotdo? Is it a g? Yes. One bold box, one awkward space. A term we can all agree on.

summary: An official notice from the department of nobody asked. Set between thin rules like real paperwork, with YOUR underlined so it sticks.

title: Heartbeat Triangle Tee
summary: One pulse, one peak. A single heartbeat runs across the chest and climbs straight into the Flavorful triangle.

title: Heartbeat Croissant Pocket Tee
summary: Vital signs: stable, slightly buttery. A tiny hand-sketched heartbeat on the pocket that settles into a croissant.

title: taco slu t Pocket Tee
summary: Loyal to one thing, and it's tacos. A small chest hit with a taco icon, finished with our woven croissant label at the hem.

summary: 8-bit appetite. A pixel-taco patch front and center, spelled exactly how we meant it.

title: no thanks Tee
summary: Polite, firm, final. A small "no thanks" up front, and the full statement on the back: not feeling emotions today.

title: Redwood Lif e Heartbeat Tee
summary: Pulse check: it's mostly trees. One thin heartbeat line wanders up into the redwoods, and the name is spelled exactly how we meant it.

title: Redwood Lif e Grove Tee
summary: Small talk up front, big trees out back. A quiet little 'redwood lif e' on the chest, and a whole grove under the moon across the shoulders.

title: Make Art With Friends Tee
summary: Three steps, no skipping. A tiny instruction sheet on the chest says find friends, make art, repeat, and out back one hand-drawn heartbeat climbs into a triangle and lands on a croissant.

title: Santa Cruz Sun Tank
summary: A 70s sunset drawn in fine lines, made for long afternoons and slow refills. Look closer: the sun is keeping a two-letter secret. Choose the printed back for a little sun and the motto, or keep the back blank.

title: Santa Cruz Dipper Tank
summary: The Giant Dipper in one tidy line drawing, with a two-letter secret hiding in the water below for people who look twice. Choose the printed back for an honest review of every coaster and most weeks, or keep the back blank.
